title: Notion vs Confluence (2026): Which Knowledge Workspace Fits?
description: Compare Notion and Confluence for team documentation, knowledge bases, collaboration, permissions, integrations, administration, and plan limits. Choose based on how your organization creates and maintains knowledge.

features.name: Primary use
features.tool1: Flexible pages, connected databases, and team knowledge
features.tool2: Team documentation and knowledge connected to Atlassian work
features.tool1Detail: Notion is worth evaluating when teams want to combine notes, structured databases, and internal knowledge in one flexible workspace. Check current capabilities: https://www.notion.so/help
features.tool2Detail: Confluence is worth evaluating when structured documentation and knowledge need to work alongside Atlassian products and team processes. Check current plans and features: https://www.atlassian.com/software/confluence

features.name: Information structure
features.tool1: Pages, nested content, and databases configured by the team
features.tool2: Spaces, pages, and structured team documentation
features.tool1Detail: Build a small knowledge base with clear ownership, navigation, and templates; test whether the structure stays understandable as content grows.
features.tool2Detail: Build representative spaces and page trees, then test navigation, ownership, permissions, and maintenance as teams and documentation expand.

features.name: Collaborative editing
features.tool2: Collaborative pages and team documentation workflows
features.tool1Detail: Test simultaneous editing, comments, version history, notifications, and how decisions are captured for your team: https://www.notion.so/help
features.tool2Detail: Test page editing, comments, version history, templates, and review workflows with the roles who will author and maintain documentation: https://support.atlassian.com/confluence-cloud/

features.name: Structured data and project context
features.tool1: Flexible databases can connect documentation with lightweight workflows
features.tool2: Structured documentation can link to Jira issues and other Atlassian work
features.tool1Detail: Prototype the databases and relationships you need, then verify filters, views, permissions, and automation in the intended plan.
features.tool2Detail: If your team uses Jira, test how pages link to issues and projects and whether the resulting documentation flow matches your process: https://www.atlassian.com/software/confluence

features.tool2: Space and page permissions depend on configuration and plan
features.tool1Detail: Test guest access, sharing defaults, admin roles, and access removal in a sample workspace. Review current security information: https://www.notion.so/security
features.tool2Detail: Test space permissions, external access, user lifecycle, and administration with representative roles. Review current security information: https://www.atlassian.com/trust/security

features.name: Integrations and search
features.tool1: Integrations and search across workspace content
features.tool2: Integrations and search across documentation and connected Atlassian work
features.tool1Detail: Test the exact integrations and search workflows your team relies on; verify that connected sources and access rules behave as expected: https://www.notion.so/help
features.tool2Detail: Test search across the spaces and tools your organization uses, and confirm how permissions affect discoverability: https://support.atlassian.com/confluence-cloud/

features.tool2: AI features and availability depend on current plan and configuration

features.tool2Detail: Identify the specific AI workflows you need and confirm current availability, data handling, and plan eligibility in Atlassian's official documentation.

features.tool1: Free and paid plans; current limits must be checked
features.tool2: Free and paid plans; current limits must be checked

features.tool2Detail: Compare seats, admin controls, collaboration features, and billing terms on the current official pricing page: https://www.atlassian.com/software/confluence/pricing

features.name: Migration and adoption
features.tool1: Flexible workspace design requires decisions about structure and ownership
features.tool2: Documentation migration may require planning for spaces, permissions, and links
features.tool1Detail: Import a representative sample of pages and databases, then test links, permissions, search, exports, and the work required to maintain the new structure.
features.tool2Detail: Import a representative set of pages and attachments, then test link integrity, permissions, search, version history, and how connected Jira content behaves.

verdict: Notion is a reasonable starting point when a team wants flexible pages and connected databases that can support both documentation and lightweight workflows. Confluence is a reasonable starting point when formal team documentation needs to connect closely with Atlassian products and established project processes. Neither is a verified universal winner. The better choice depends on the knowledge structure you need, who maintains it, how permissions work, and which integrations matter. Before migrating, test a representative set of pages, search, access controls, exports, version history, and links to existing work. Compare current plan limits and security terms on the official vendor pages rather than relying on old price or rating claims.

faqs.question: Is Notion or Confluence better for a company wiki?
faqs.answer: Both can support team knowledge. Notion suits teams that want flexible pages and databases, while Confluence may fit teams that organize documentation around spaces and Atlassian work. Test search, ownership, permissions, templates, and maintenance with your actual content.

faqs.question: Which is better for technical documentation?
faqs.answer: The answer depends on how your team writes, reviews, and links documentation to development work. If your process relies on Jira and established Atlassian workflows, test Confluence's fit. If you want flexible pages and connected databases, test Notion against the same requirements.

faqs.question: Can Notion replace Confluence?
faqs.answer: It may fit teams whose documentation and database workflows map well to Notion. Before replacing Confluence, test migration of pages and attachments, link integrity, permissions, search, version history, and any Jira-linked workflows.

faqs.question: Can Confluence replace Notion?
faqs.answer: It may fit teams centered on structured documentation and Atlassian work. Teams that depend on flexible databases or customized workspace structures should prototype those workflows in Confluence before migrating.

faqs.question: Which is cheaper?
faqs.answer: Pricing and included features can change by plan, region, billing term, and seat count. Compare the current official pricing pages and include the admin, collaboration, and AI features you actually need.

faqs.question: Which has better integrations?
faqs.answer: The better fit depends on your existing tools. Test the specific integrations and permission behavior your team relies on, rather than comparing the number of integrations alone.

faqs.question: What should we test before migrating a knowledge base?
faqs.answer: Import a representative set of pages and attachments. Verify links, search, access controls, comments, version history, exports, templates, and who will own updates after the migration.

faqs.question: How should a team choose between them?
faqs.answer: Write down the knowledge workflows you need, test them in both products, confirm the current plan and security terms, and involve the people who will create and maintain the content. Do not rely on an unverified overall rating to make the decision.
